task: Keep the global Proof-or-Stop executable working after dist rebuilds and make its diagnostics and evidence portable across POSIX and Windows hosts.
outcome: After npm --prefix packages/main run build, the regression prints contract: global-cli-bin-target-restored and proof-or-stop --version succeeds. A healthy proof-or-stop doctor prints contract: global-core-realpath-pass only when the package, PATH command, bin target, compiled version, and host executable contract agree; otherwise it prints a host-valid repair command.
facts: TypeScript emits fresh POSIX dist entrypoints without executable bits.
The global executable may be a POSIX symlink or a Windows npm command shim targeting packages/main/dist/cli.js.
promoteDist validates the staging package manifest and declared bin targets before old-dist eviction.
Only a missing or syntactically invalid package manifest and ENOENT target are benign; other read, stat, realpath, or chmod errors must fail closed.
Final and intermediate symlink escapes must be rejected both during promotion and in doctor bin-target inspection.
POSIX validates executable access; Windows validates the actual PATH-selected npm command shim rather than POSIX mode bits.
A healthy global npm package cannot substitute for a missing proof-or-stop command on PATH.
A failed compiled-version probe is not evidence for the package manifest version.
constraints: Use only node: built-ins in scripts/promote-dist.mjs.
Preserve atomic promotion and leave the old dist intact when staging validation fails.
Doctor remains read-only and emits POSIX shell remediation on POSIX or encoded PowerShell LiteralPath remediation on Windows.
Capability skips cannot emit the must PASS selector before non-link assertions execute.
Story metadata and implementation remain English.
Do not expand scope for unrelated medium or low defects; record evidence and route them to an explicit later owner.
